display_name: The monthly net income of an employed parent in Israel, composed from the Income Tax Ordinance and the National Insurance Law
citation: A composed subject. Instruments: Income Tax Ordinance [New Version] (דמ״י תשכ״א, 120; subject il/income-tax-ordinance-new-version) and National Insurance Law [Consolidated Version], 5755-1995 (ס״ח תשנ״ה, 210; subject il/national-insurance-law-consolidated-version-5755-1995). Rows composed: legalese-2026-10-il-01 (ITO ss 33A, 34, 36, 36A), legalese-2026-10-il-02 (ITO s 66), legalese-2026-10-il-03 (ITO ss 120B, 121, 121B), legalese-2026-10-il-04 (NII s 1 as needed, ss 334, 337, Schedule J), legalese-2026-10-il-05 (NII Schedule K, ss 342, 348), legalese-2026-10-il-06 (NII ss 65-68), and from encoding version 0.2.0 legalese-2026-10-il-08 in both subjects (ITO ss 35, 37-39, 40(b), 45A, 47, 64B, 65; NII s 72, s 335, Schedule A1 Part D).
authority: The Knesset, as the enacting authority of both instruments. The composition itself is not law.

source.note: No source text of its own. The two instruments' Hebrew texts are deposited in their own subjects' registers/source-bundle/ (unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidations, as amended at retrieval on 2026-10-06), with the NII amending Laws in registers/source-bundle/amending-laws/. The composed encoding quotes them for checking only; every rule it applies is a row's.

not_law_note: THIS SUBJECT IS NOT A STATUTE. It is a question - what is the monthly net income, in a month of 2026, of an employed parent with children? - answered by composing encodings of two statutes (six in encoding version 0.1.0, eight from 0.2.0), each deposited under its own statute's subject. An encoding here owns no rule of law: it owns its household nouns, its adapters between the rows, its named refusals where no row reaches, and its forks where the text does not decide how the rows meet (annual tax against a month, which tax year's additional tax excludes a parent from the allowance, and the like). The leaf slug names the question rather than an enactment year, because there is no enactment.
